land.text: the Thanjavur country, governed by Sevappa Nayaka for Vijayanagara before 1532

predecessors.note: Thanjavur Nayak page: after the Chola collapse of 1279 Thanjavur passed to the Pandyas and later to Vijayanagara in the late 14th century. The vijayanagara-empire dossier records the vassalage from 1534 and its end at 1565 (a bridge).

land.text: the Thanjavur country, taken by Venkoji (Ekoji I) in 1675

successors.note: The thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier (sa-05) dates the founding to early 1676 and has the Nayak state as predecessor; Cliopatria's Maratha row starts 1677.

capitals.name: Thanjavur (Tanjore)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Thanjavur; the Raghunatha page names no other seat.

rulers.name: Achuthappa Nayaka
rulers.note: r. 1560-1614 on the page, co-regent with Sevappa until 1580; the strip shows the sole reign.

rulers.name: Raghunatha Nayaka
rulers.note: Ascended in 1600 and ruled with his father until 1614, then alone; died 1634.

rulers.name: Vijaya Raghava Nayaka
rulers.note: Fell in the battle of the siege of Thanjavur in 1673 (the page does not name his death directly). No ruler is named for 1673-1675.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1532-1533: Cliopatria's row begins in 1534, but the page has Achyuta Deva Raya in 1532 granting Sevappa Nayaka permission to establish a hereditary feudatory kingdom (infobox 'Established' 1532, founding 'around 1532'). The 1534 shape is used unchanged.

14,610 km2 round Thanjavur (Kumbakonam, Kollidam country). The page gives no area and no boundary; its only territorial reference is a map caption, 'Approximate extent of the Thanjavur Nayaka Kingdom, c. 1572'. An inscription of 1556 names Sevappa as governing Thanjavur. Unverified beyond that.

14,694 km2, the same polygon (two cells more). The page's map is dated c. 1572; the Raghunatha Nayak page puts the Kollidam rebel Solaga's island fortress inside the kingdom (c. 1616), Tranquebar on the coast (1620), and Pazhamaneri (August 1616) on its roads. The page gives no boundary, so the shape stands.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, for 1673-1675; the land is occupied by Madurai (ledger) and taken by Venkoji in 1675

keyframe_review.note: The row runs to 1676 but the page has the siege of Thanjavur by Chokkanatha of Madurai in 1673 (infobox 'Disestablished' 1673), Madurai briefly ruled the city until 1675 and Venkoji capturing Thanjavur in 1675. The shape stands for 1673-1675 as Thanjavur's land under a Madurai occupation (ledger); 1676 belongs to the Maratha dossier.

ledger.note: 1532: Achyuta Deva Raya lets his governor Sevappa Nayaka found a hereditary kingdom at Thanjavur. In 1532 CE, Achyuta Deva Raya 'granted regional governor Sevappa Nayaka permission to establish a hereditary feudatory kingdom'; Cliopatria starts the row in 1534.

1673: Chokkanatha Nayaka of Madurai besieges Thanjavur and Vijaya Raghava dies in the battle. Page: the siege of Thanjavur in 1673; Madurai briefly ruled the city until 1675 (infobox 'Disestablished' 1673). Madurai's own dossier records the same occupation.
1675: Madurai's hold ends when Venkoji takes Thanjavur (page: the Maratha conquest of 1675; Madurai ruled the city until 1675).

1675: Venkoji (Ekoji I) captures Thanjavur. Page: Venkoji (Ekoji I) captured Thanjavur in 1675 and founded the Thanjavur Maratha Kingdom. The thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier has him defeating Alagiri and taking power in early 1676.

1675: the Nayak kingdom of Thanjavur ends in the Maratha conquest. The infobox ends the dynasty in 1673 with Vijaya Raghava's fall; the land stays the Nayak state's under Madurai's occupation until Venkoji takes it in 1675.

wars.name: Battle of Vallamprakara (Thanjavur against Madurai)
wars.outcome: Thanjavur troops, allied with Aravidu imperial forces, defeated the army of Virappa Nayaka of Madurai. No border moved.
wars.note: Undated on the page; 1572-1595 is Virappa's reign on the Madurai Nayak page (opened for the Madurai dossier), so the years are a bridge.

wars.name: Battle of Toppur
wars.outcome: On 12 December 1616 Raghunatha was 'completely victorious'; Jaggaraya was killed and Rama Deva Raya was put on the throne (crowned at Kumbakonam in early 1617). The Madurai Nayak page has Muttu Virappa moving his capital to Tiruchirappalli that year. No Thanjavur border moved.
wars.note: The Thanjavur Nayak page calls Toppur a victory of Raghunatha's loyalist forces over a rebel coalition (late 1616).

wars.name: Thanjavur's Jaffna expeditions
wars.outcome: Cankili II, placed on the Jaffna throne by Thanjavur forces, was overthrown and killed in 1619; Raghunatha sent five armies to conquer Jaffna in 1619-1621 and all failed. No land was held.

wars.name: Siege of Thanjavur (1673)
wars.outcome: Chokkanatha Nayaka of Madurai besieged Thanjavur in 1673 and Vijaya Raghava died in the battle; Madurai held the city until 1675.

wars.name: Maratha conquest of Thanjavur
wars.outcome: Venkoji (Ekoji I) captured Thanjavur in 1675 and founded the Thanjavur Maratha Kingdom.
wars.note: The page has no 1676 date; the thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier has early 1676.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary, only a c. 1572 map caption; the Kollidam and the coast are the only natural limits named on the pages opened.

sources.title: Thanjavur Nayak kingdom
sources.note: Founding 1532, rulers, independence after 1565 (undated), Toppur, the siege of 1673, the Maratha conquest of 1675. No area.

sources.title: Raghunatha Nayak
sources.note: Raghunatha's reign 1600-1634: Toppur 12 December 1616, Jaffna 1619-1621, Tranquebar 1620.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Nayaks of Thanjavur' 1534-1676 (3 shapes of 14,610 to 14,694 km2, one polygon with two cells of difference). The page gives no area and no boundary (only a c. 1572 map caption), so the shapes are kept as ok and the dossier rests on the founding (1532), the end (1673 siege; 1675 Venkoji) and the rulers.
Page conflicts: the Thanjavur Nayak page infobox ends the kingdom in 1673 (Vijaya Raghava's fall) but says Madurai briefly ruled the city until 1675 and Venkoji captured Thanjavur in 1675; Cliopatria runs to 1676; the thanjavur-maratha-kingdom dossier (another agent) has Venkoji defeating Alagiri at Ayyampet and taking power in early 1676. This dossier keeps the Nayak state to 1675, with Madurai's 1673-1675 hold as an occupation (the nayaks-of-madurai dossier records the same), so the Maratha dossier's founding in 1676 from this state fits. Alagiri does not appear on the two pages opened. No page dates the independence from Vijayanagara ('increasing autonomy ... after 1565'); the vijayanagara-empire dossier bridges the end of the vassalage at 1565. The Vallamprakara battle against Madurai is undated. Tranquebar (Danish post of 20 November 1620, Ove Gjedde) is a trading lease and not drawn. Not on the pages opened: Bijapur's pressure in the 1650s, Mysore, the Tondaiman and Kallar chiefs, Nagapattinam and Karaikal, Vijaya Raghava's reign events, the Portuguese and Dutch. Pages opened: 2 (budget 1-2): Thanjavur Nayak kingdom, Raghunatha Nayak. The Madurai Nayak page (opened for the Madurai dossier) supplies the Madurai side of 1673-1675.
Counterparts: vijayanagara-empire (founding), nayaks-of-madurai (occupation 1673-1675), thanjavur-maratha-kingdom (1675). Needing dossiers: the Jaffna kingdom (a Cliopatria row, jaffna-kingdom, 1314-1594) is only a belligerent here.
Gazetteer: Thanjavur and Kumbakonam are present; the Kollidam is not used.
